_doc: Speech calls that do not write braille in the same function, each reviewed: 'delegates' (hands the text to something that mirrors) or 'speech_only' (why braille cannot or need not follow). Generated by python -m quill.tools.braille_parity_audit --write; kinds and reasons are written by a person.

quill/apps/lite_shell_menu.py::ShellMenu.reason: The empty window speaks through the same QUILL Lite voice as a document window: ScreenReaderVoice.speak (quill/apps/lite_voice.py) writes the text to braille straight after the speech.

quill/apps/lite_window.py::DocumentFrame.reason: QUILL Lite's voice: ScreenReaderVoice.speak (quill/apps/lite_voice.py) writes the same text to braille through the coalescer straight after the speech goes out.

quill/platform/windows/prism_bridge.py::.reason: The system voice speaks only when no screen reader is running, and a braille display is driven by a screen reader: there is nothing to write to.

Narrator: the message goes to Narrator as a UI Automation notification, and Narrator puts its notifications on its own braille display. Neither Prism nor accessible_output2 has a braille route into Narrator, so writing it again is not possible.
macOS self-voice runs only when VoiceOver is off; without VoiceOver no braille display is driven.
VoiceOver shows announcement notifications on its braille display itself; QUILL writing them as well would show each twice.

quill/ui/app_shell.py::AppShellFrame._an.reason: Only when no announcement service was built: the engine's own inline braille is still on then (only the service's wiring switches it off), so AnnouncementEngine.announce mirrors the message itself.
